title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-04-02
content:
Morning notes:
- Standup: focused on KV cache thrash in 40B model runs.
- Observed increased p99 ~45% on dedicated pool during burst 09:10-09:35 UTC. Kernel logs show repeated cache invalidations.

Bug triage:
1) SERV-7893: KV cache eviction incorrectly using global LRU across shards -> hot-shard thrash.
- Repro steps: ./bench/run_seqlen.sh --model redwood-40b --concurrency 32 --prefix-length 32
- Hypothesis: eviction policy uses global LRU counter with shard-local timestamps; race under concurrency.
- Next: add unit test for eviction ordering; instrument eviction with per-shard timestamps. Assigned to Priya.

2) GH #1419: fused-attn kernel returns NaNs for seqlen=4096 in bf16 path. 2/100 failures observed.
- Quick fix: fallback to generic kernel for bf16 if NaNs detected; longer-term: patch numeric stability in softmax.
- PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1423 (WIP)

Perf TODOs:
- Run 3x stable benchmarks on dedicated-staging (g5-16x) after PR 1423 merges. Cmd: 
  ./tools/bench.sh --model redwood-40b --batch 8 --seq 2048 --runs 3 --pool dedicated-staging
- Add p50/p90/p99 columns to perf dashboard for per-model sequence-length buckets.
- Experiment: adaptive batching window=12ms vs 20ms for small-prefix traffic; measure cost delta and latency distribution.

Kernel notes:
- Suspect accumulation buffer alignment issue causing bf16 fallback; check loads at fused_attn.cu: line ~723.
- TODO: add aligned_malloc / __align__ checks and unit tests for unaligned tensors.
- Note: vectorized loads assume 16-byte alignment; add guards for odd-shaped tensors.

Deployment / rollout:
- Canary plan: deploy fused-attn fix to canary pool (10% capacity) with auto-rollback if error rate > 0.5% or latency spike > 20%.
- Coordinate with SRE (Miguel) to schedule canary tonight 02:00 UTC.

Misc:
- Update changelog + release notes for Dedicated (include kv-cache eviction fix + fused-attn fallback).
- Follow-up: meeting with product about exposing 'eviction_policy' in console (A/B test LRU vs LFU) next Wed.
- Instrumentation: add metric 'serving.kv_cache.evictions' (per-shard) and 'serving.kv_cache.eviction_latency_ms'.

Afternoon plan:
- 13:00: pair with Priya on unit test for eviction ordering.
- 15:00: run extended perf (6h) on dedicated-staging, collect bucketed tail latencies.
- 17:30: write up triage notes for CS with customer impact summary + mitigation steps.

Unresolved questions:
- Is global LRU required for correctness (consistency guarantees) or can we move to per-shard LFU to improve tail?
- Should we disable prefetch for prefixes >1024 temporarily to reduce KV pressure? Quick experiment?

Commands / quick refs:
- Repro bench: ./bench/run_seqlen.sh --model redwood-40b --concurrency 32 --prefix-length 32 --pool dedicated-staging
- Local run for fused-attn: docker-compose run bench /usr/local/bin/run_fused_attn_test --seq 4096 --dtype bf16
- Inspect logs: ./tools/agg_logs.py --from 2026-04-02T09:00 --to 2026-04-02T09:40 --service serving-runtime

Notes to self: "instrument serving-metrics with eviction_count per-shard" and follow up with infra to add taggable dimensions (region, pool, model).
